question: I cast Rancor targeting my only creature, and in response my opponent destroys that creature. When Rancor ends up in my graveyard, does its ability return it to my hand?

expected.shortAnswer: No: Rancor's target is illegal when it tries to resolve, so the Aura spell doesn't resolve, never enters the battlefield, and its return-to-hand ability doesn't trigger.
expected.answer: If the creature this Aura would enchant is an illegal target by the time Rancor tries to resolve, the Aura spell doesn't resolve. It won't enter the battlefield, so it won't be put into a graveyard from the battlefield and its ability won't trigger.

whyHard: Rancor really does land in the graveyard, so players assume its return trigger fires, but a fizzled Aura spell never touched the battlefield.
